year, month, day, carrier_code, flight_number, and origin_code are all required columns with null_rate 0.0 in the profile and together plausibly identify one scheduled flight per day per origin, forming the smallest defensible grain.

This proposal's schema allows only one source column per action, so year (distinct_count 1), month (distinct_count 6), and day (distinct_count 31) could not be merged into a single DATE column as the operator's team convention prefers; a human should merge them downstream.

departure_time (null_rate 0.029388), departure_delay_minutes (null_rate 0.029388), arrival_time (null_rate 0.0307), arrival_delay_minutes (null_rate 0.032981), and air_time_minutes (null_rate 0.032981) all carry nonzero null rates consistent with flights that never departed or arrived, so nulls are retained rather than imputed.
Operator context states a flight that never departed has no departure time, and dep_time shows null_count 4883 (null_rate 0.029388), so is_cancelled is derived as true when departure_time is null.
tailnum has null_count 1521 (null_rate 0.009154), a small but nonzero rate, so the renamed tail_number column stays nullable rather than failing the build.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true in the profile, so they are dropped as pipeline capture artifacts, not business data.

departure_time, scheduled_departure_time, arrival_time, and scheduled_arrival_time use HHMM/HMM packed integer encoding per operator context (e.g. max 2400.0, min 1.0) rather than true time values, so they are cast to INTEGER rather than a TIME or TIMESTAMP type.

purpose: This table holds cleaned, typed, flight-level records drawn from the nycflights13 flights table: every reported January-June 2013 departure from JFK, LGA, and EWR, feeding downstream analysis of on-time performance, delays, and carrier operations.
usage: Read departure_time, scheduled_departure_time, arrival_time, and scheduled_arrival_time as packed HHMM/HMM local-time integers, not true time or timestamp values; join on carrier_code, flight_number, origin_code, and the date parts (year, month, day) as the declared grain; filter or branch on is_cancelled before computing delay statistics, since departure_delay_minutes, arrival_delay_minutes, air_time_minutes, and departure_time/arrival_time are null exactly when a flight never departed or arrived.
limitations: year, month, and day remain three separate INTEGER columns rather than one DATE column because this cleanup pass's schema permits only one source column per target; a human should merge them downstream per the operator's calendar-date convention. tail_number (null_rate 0.009154), departure/arrival times and delays (null_rate 0.0294-0.033), and air_time_minutes (null_rate 0.032981) retain nulls rather than being imputed, so consumers must handle them explicitly. No exact duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0), so no dedupe logic was applied.
